investigation: Cliffside Park New Jersey public property-tax rate comparison

comparison.interpretation: The general rate increased by $0.080 per $100 of assessed value; the effective statistical rate fell by $0.046 per $100. Neither metric alone establishes changes to an individual parcel's tax bill.

nextMissingLinks.needed: Dated and legally public block/lot or property identifier with tax assessment; no individual resident names
Parcel-specific legally assessed bill, adjustments and appeal information
Tax collector's posted payments and credits, with payer/escrow PII redacted
Project-specific PILOT or tax-abatement agreement and annual service charge, if applicable
Municipal audited cash receipts vs budget estimate, school and county allocation
Official adopted ordinance, minutes, vote or tax decision and its effective date
Verified property titleholder and separately documented company-control relationship
Exact campaign or lobbying filing matched to legal filer and decision period
Comparable lease or asking-rent observations plus admissible counterfactual

safeguards: General property-tax rate, effective statistical rate, assessed value, tax bill, payment and municipal cash collection are distinct.
A rate change does not imply a household tax bill rose by the same percentage; assessed values and adjustments may change.
No property, person, beneficial owner, political donation, PILOT beneficiary, corruption or rent effect has been inferred from these municipal rates.
The source files were inspected through public official pages, not archived. Original-file SHA-256 not captured; citation links preserve the page and table row.
